title: Phytochemical profile of bioactive Siraitia grosvenorii root fraction and its potential against nonsmall cell lung cancer in vitro and in vivo.
authors: Wei, Yulu; Jiang, Xiaohua; Song, Jingru; Yan, Xiaojie; Zhang, Jie; Dong, Fei; Li, Dianpeng; Liu, Hongwei; Lu, Fenglai
one_liner_zh: 该文研究罗汉果根活性成分对非小细胞肺癌的抑制作用，涉及分子对接但对象为化合物-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD方法，与本课题关联极弱。
abstract: Siraitia grosvenorii (Swingle) C. Jeffrey (SG) is an edible medicinal plant traditionally used to alleviate pulmonary and intestinal diseases in China. Rising demand for SG has led to significant generation of discarded SG roots (SGRs), while previous studies have shown that SGR extract possesses antiproliferative activity against cancer cells. However, its therapeutic potential for nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and underlying molecular mechanisms remain uncharacterized. In this study, liquid chromatography ion trap time-of-flight mass spectrometry analysis identified 26 constituents from the active fraction of SGR (SGR2), predominantly categorized as cucurbitane or nor-cucurbitane triterpenoids and their glycosides. SGR2 inhibited the proliferation of A549 cells by inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest. In a xenograft tumor model, low-dose SGR2 treatment significantly suppressed tumor growth while exhibiting no observable adverse effects. RNA-seq analysis revealed that SGR2 impacted multiple targets and key pathways relevant to cancer therapy, notably including the JAK/STAT pathway. Western blotting analysis confirmed that SGR2 inhibited the JAK2/STAT3 pathway by reducing phosphorylation expression of JAK2 and STAT3 in both in vitro and in vivo models, and molecular docking studies demonstrated strong binding affinities between active compounds and key target proteins. These findings underscore the remarkable efficacy of SG byproducts and demonstrate their potential applications in NSCLC treatment. The results also contribute to the enhanced productivity and sustainability of SG cultivation.
abstract_zh: 罗汉果（Siraitia grosvenorii (Swingle) C. Jeffrey，SG）是一种药食两用植物，在中国传统上用于缓解肺部和肠道疾病。随着对SG需求的增加，废弃罗汉果根（SGRs）大量产生，而先前研究表明SGR提取物具有抗癌细胞增殖活性。然而，其对非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）的治疗潜力及潜在分子机制尚未明确。本研究通过液相色谱离子阱飞行时间质谱分析，从SGR活性组分（SGR2）中鉴定出26种成分，主要归类为葫芦素烷型或降葫芦素烷型三萜及其糖苷。SGR2通过诱导细胞凋亡和细胞周期阻滞抑制A549细胞增殖。在异种移植肿瘤模型中，低剂量SGR2处理显著抑制肿瘤生长，且未观察到明显不良反应。RNA-seq分析显示，SGR2影响与癌症治疗相关的多个靶点和关键通路，尤其包括JAK/STAT通路。Western blotting分析证实，在体外和体内模型中，SGR2通过降低JAK2和STAT3的磷酸化表达来抑制JAK2/STAT3通路，分子对接研究显示活性化合物与关键靶蛋白之间具有强结合亲和力。这些发现凸显了SG副产物的显著功效，并展示了其在NSCLC治疗中的潜在应用。研究结果也有助于提高SG种植的生产力和可持续性。
